angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 260,192 km at 159.16 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.2828 +/- 0.0298 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 159.16 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.374 +/- 0.089 solar radii from Kruse et al. 2019, the stellar radius of EPIC 201238110 b's parameter set from Kruse et al. 2019 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJS..244...11K/abstract): 260,192 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.41 +/- 0.112 solar masses from Heller et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of EPIC 201238110 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...627A..66H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3587 +/- 157 K from Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the effective temperature of TIC 35019000 (VizieR IV/39/tic82); no NASA Exoplanet Archive row gives one (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ab3467). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the effective temperature of TIC 35019000 (VizieR IV/39/tic82); no NASA Exoplanet Archive row gives one (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ab3467)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/epic-201238110.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.905, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
